title: Infosys Shares Fall 4% After Q2: Brokerages Split Between Buy And Hold
excerpt: UBS sees 23% upside to Rs 1,415 while Goldman Sachs targets Rs 1,000 as Infosys cuts FY27 guidance to 1-2% after its September quarter
body:
• Infosys shares fell 4 per cent on Monday, October 26, after the company cut its FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance to 1-2 per cent from 1.5-3 per cent following its September quarter results.
  • Brokerages are split: UBS (Buy, Rs 1,415) and Nomura and Motilal Oswal (Buy, Rs 1,300) see upside, while Goldman Sachs (Neutral, Rs 1,000), HSBC (Hold, Rs 1,110) and Citi (Neutral, Rs 1,105) are cautious.
  • For investors: the stock closed at Rs 1,153.80 on Friday before the results, so the published targets span from about 13 per cent below that close at Goldman Sachs to about 23 per cent above it at UBS.
  • Positives cited by analysts include $5.2 billion in large deals and 29 per cent sequential growth in AI services revenue, against pressure from weak client spending and second-half wage hikes.

Infosys shares fell 4 per cent on Monday after India's second-largest IT services company cut its full-year revenue outlook for a second straight quarter, prompting a divided response from brokerages over whether the sell-off is a buying opportunity or a signal to stay cautious.

The Bengaluru-based company lowered its FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance to 1-2 per cent, from 1.5-3 per cent, citing sluggish client spending and subdued volume growth. It retained its operating margin guidance at 20-22 per cent. The stock had closed at Rs 1,153.80 on Friday and has fallen 28.2 per cent so far in 2026, according to Moneycontrol reporting via TradingView.

What the September quarter showed

Infosys reported consolidated net profit of Rs 7,823 crore for the July-September quarter, up 6.2 per cent year on year, while revenue rose 10.7 per cent to Rs 49,244 crore. Operating profit rose 10.4 per cent to Rs 10,330 crore but missed expectations, and operating margin slipped 10 basis points sequentially to 21 per cent.

Measured in constant currency, revenue grew 1.2 per cent quarter on quarter. UBS said that was below its estimate of 1.5 per cent and consensus of 1.8 per cent, while reported earnings per share of Rs 19.3 were below its estimate of Rs 19.5 and consensus of Rs 19.7. The Hindu BusinessLine reported that Goldman Sachs described the revised guidance as the second consecutive quarterly cut and said its midpoint implies modestly negative organic revenue growth for FY27.

The buy case: valuation and deal wins

UBS maintained its Buy rating with a target price of Rs 1,415, implying about 23 per cent upside from Friday's close, even though it called the second-quarter performance weaker than expected. Nomura also maintained Buy at Rs 1,300, describing the quarter as a modest miss but highlighting strong deal wins, and noted the stock was trading at 14.2 times its FY28 forecast earnings per share of Rs 81. Motilal Oswal reiterated Buy at Rs 1,300 as well.

The deal numbers underpin that case. Infosys secured large deals worth $5.2 billion in the quarter, up from $3.6 billion in the previous quarter, with 62 per cent from net-new business. AI services revenue grew 29 per cent sequentially and rose to 10.5 per cent of total revenue, from 8.2 per cent in the June quarter. HSBC, despite its Hold rating, identified a $2 billion mega deal as a positive that could contribute about one percentage point to revenue growth in FY28.

The hold and neutral case: growth and margins

HSBC retained Hold at Rs 1,110, implying about 4 per cent downside from Friday's close, saying the revised guidance puts Infosys at the lower end of its peer group and warning that margins could come under pressure in the second half because of wage hikes. Goldman Sachs maintained Neutral at Rs 1,000, citing sluggish demand, client-specific ramp-downs and pricing pressure amid elevated competition, while noting that strong deal wins should partly cushion a FY28 headwind from the exit of a manufacturing client.

Citi maintained Neutral at Rs 1,105, saying revenue and EBIT were largely in line and total contract value above $5 billion was strong. Jefferies kept Hold but lowered its target to Rs 1,140 from Rs 1,160, saying growth concerns should limit scope for a valuation re-rating. Kotak maintained Add with a fair value of Rs 1,200, citing a weak growth profile and sharp revenue declines in retail and hi-tech.

What investors should watch next

The spread of targets, from Rs 1,000 to Rs 1,415 around a Rs 1,153.80 pre-results close, shows analysts agree on the facts but not on what happens next. Bulls are pricing in conversion of the $5.2 billion deal pipeline and AI growth into FY28 revenue. Cautious brokerages are focused on whether client spending recovers, whether wage hikes compress the 20-22 per cent margin band, and whether guidance is cut again. The next test is execution against the lowered 1-2 per cent range itself.
